name: Classic Margherita Pizza
summary: A traditional Neapolitan pizza with a hand-stretched base, bright tomato sauce, fresh mozzarella, and basil. Deceptively simple and endlessly satisfying.
ingredients: Large handful of fresh basil leaves

steps.action: Combine yeast, sugar, and warm water. Let sit 5 minutes until frothy.
Add flour, salt, and olive oil to the yeast mixture. Mix until a shaggy dough forms, then knead on a floured surface for 8–10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Shape dough into a ball, place in an oiled bowl, cover with a damp cloth, and leave to rise in a warm spot for 1 hour until doubled in size.
Crush canned tomatoes by hand into a bowl. Season with salt, a pinch of oregano, and a drizzle of olive oil. Do not cook.
Preheat oven to its highest setting (250–280°C) with the baking tray inside for at least 30 minutes.
Stretch the dough by hand into a thin round. Spread tomato sauce, tear over the mozzarella, and slide onto the hot tray.
Bake for 10–12 minutes until the crust is charred at the edges and cheese is bubbling. Finish with fresh basil and a drizzle of extra-virgin olive oil.

variants.name: Vegan
variants.description: All the classic pizza flavour without any animal products — vegan mozzarella melts beautifully and nutritional yeast adds a subtle umami depth.
ingredients: Large handful of fresh basil leaves

steps.action: Combine yeast, sugar, and warm water. Let sit 5 minutes until frothy.
Add flour, salt, and olive oil to the yeast mixture. Mix until a shaggy dough forms, then knead on a floured surface for 8–10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Shape dough into a ball, place in an oiled bowl, cover with a damp cloth, and leave to rise for 1 hour until doubled in size.
Crush canned tomatoes by hand into a bowl. Season with salt, a pinch of oregano, and a drizzle of olive oil. Keep it rough and chunky.
Preheat oven to its highest setting (250–280°C) with the baking tray inside for 30 minutes.
Stretch the dough by hand into a thin round. Spread tomato sauce, tear over the vegan mozzarella, and sprinkle with nutritional yeast.
Bake for 10–12 minutes until the crust is charred at the edges. Scatter basil and finish with a drizzle of extra-virgin olive oil.

name: Avocado & Tomato Salad
summary: A bright, no-cook salad of creamy avocado, juicy cherry tomatoes, and cool cucumber in a zingy lemon-herb dressing. On the table in 15 minutes.
ingredients: Small handful of fresh cilantro or parsley
Salt and black pepper to taste

steps.action: Whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, cumin, salt, and pepper in a small bowl. Set aside.
Halve, pit, and dice the avocados. Halve the cherry tomatoes. Dice the cucumber. Thinly slice the red onion.
Combine all vegetables in a salad bowl. Pour over the dressing and toss gently. Scatter cilantro and chilli flakes on top and serve immediately.

name: Lemon Garlic Grilled Salmon
summary: Salmon fillets marinated in garlic, lemon, and herbs then grilled until perfectly flaky. A fast weeknight dinner that feels special.
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
Lemon wedges and dill to serve

steps.action: Mix garlic, lemon juice, lemon zest, olive oil, dill, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper in a small bowl.
Pat salmon dry, place in a dish, and brush all over with the marinade. Rest for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Heat grill pan over high heat until smoking. Place salmon skin-side down and cook 4 minutes without moving. Flip and cook 2–3 minutes more until just cooked through.
Rest for 2 minutes. Serve with lemon wedges and fresh dill.
ingredients: lemon wedges and dill to serve

name: Creamy Mushroom Pasta
summary: Silky pasta ribbons coated in a rich garlic-cream sauce with golden sautéed mushrooms and parmesan. A comforting bowl ready in 30 minutes.

steps.action: Bring a large pot of heavily salted water to a boil.

Slice mushrooms thickly. Heat butter and olive oil in a wide pan over high heat. Add mushrooms in a single layer — don't stir for 3 minutes so they brown properly. Toss, season, and cook 2 more minutes.
Add garlic and thyme to the mushrooms, cook 1 minute. Pour in the white wine and let it bubble and reduce by half, about 2 minutes.
Cook pasta in the boiling water until 1 minute before al dente. Reserve 1 cup of pasta water before draining.

Add cream to the mushroom pan, simmer 3 minutes. Add pasta and parmesan, tossing vigorously and adding splashes of pasta water to achieve a glossy, coating sauce. Serve with extra parmesan and parsley.

name: Chocolate Chip Cookies
summary: Chewy-centred, slightly crisp-edged cookies with pools of melted chocolate. The browned butter and extra yolk give them a bakery-level depth of flavour.
ingredients: 300g dark chocolate chips or roughly chopped chocolate

steps.action: Brown the butter: melt in a saucepan over medium heat, stirring until it smells nutty and turns amber, about 5 minutes. Pour into a large bowl and let cool 10 minutes.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Line baking sheets with parchment.
Whisk both sugars into the cooled brown butter until combined. Add eggs, extra yolk, and vanilla; whisk vigorously for 1 minute until pale and thick.
Fold in flour, baking soda, and salt until just combined. Stir in chocolate chips.
Scoop 2-tablespoon balls of dough onto the prepared sheets, spacing 5cm apart. Sprinkle with flaky sea salt. Bake 11–13 minutes until edges are set but centres still look underdone.
Cool on the tray for 5 minutes — they firm up as they cool. Transfer to a wire rack.

name: Shakshuka
summary: Eggs gently poached in a bold, spiced tomato and pepper sauce. A North African and Middle Eastern staple that works equally well for breakfast, lunch, or dinner.
ingredients: Crusty bread or pita to serve
tools: Large oven-safe skillet or frying pan

steps.action: Heat olive oil in the skillet over medium heat. Add onion and pepper, cook 7–8 minutes until softened and starting to caramelise.
tools: Large oven-safe skillet or frying pan

steps.action: Add garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, coriander, and cayenne. Stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
tools: Large oven-safe skillet or frying pan

steps.action: Pour in the crushed tomatoes. Season generously with salt and pepper. Simmer over medium-low heat for 10 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
tools: Large oven-safe skillet or frying pan

steps.action: Make 4 wells in the sauce. Crack one egg into each well. Cover with a lid and cook 5–7 minutes until whites are set but yolks are still runny.
tools: Large oven-safe skillet or frying pan

steps.action: Scatter with fresh herbs and crumbled feta. Serve directly from the pan with crusty bread.

name: Red Lentil Soup
summary: A warming, golden soup packed with protein-rich red lentils, aromatic spices, and a hit of lemon. Vegan, cheap, and effortlessly good.
ingredients: Fresh parsley and chilli flakes to serve

steps.action: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add onion and carrot, cook 8 minutes until softened.
Add garlic, cumin, turmeric, and paprika. Stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the rinsed lentils, diced tomatoes, and vegetable stock. Bring to a boil then reduce to a steady simmer.
Simmer for 20–25 minutes until lentils are completely soft and beginning to dissolve.
Use an immersion blender to partially blend the soup — blitz half to create a creamy texture while leaving some whole lentils. Stir in lemon juice, adjust seasoning.
Ladle into bowls. Top with a drizzle of olive oil, fresh parsley, and chilli flakes. Serve with warm bread.

name: Banana Oat Pancakes
summary: Fluffy, naturally sweet pancakes made from ripe bananas and oats — no refined flour, no refined sugar. Vegan-friendly and ready in 20 minutes.
ingredients: Coconut oil or neutral oil for frying
Fresh berries, maple syrup, or nut butter to serve

steps.action: Add oats, bananas, plant milk, baking powder, cinnamon, vanilla, and salt to a blender. Blend until completely smooth. Let the batter rest 5 minutes.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium-low heat with a little coconut oil. Pour in ¼ cup of batter per pancake. Cook 3 minutes until bubbles form on the surface and edges look set.
Flip and cook a further 2 minutes until golden. Repeat with remaining batter. Serve stacked with fresh berries and maple syrup.
ingredients: fresh berries, maple syrup, or nut butter

name: Spaghetti Bolognese
summary: A slow-cooked meat ragù from Bologna, built on a soffritto base with wine, milk, and a long, gentle simmer. Time-consuming but deeply rewarding.
tools: Large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven

steps.action: Heat olive oil over medium heat. Add onion, carrot, and celery (the soffritto). Cook, stirring frequently, for 12–15 minutes until very soft and lightly golden.
tools: Large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven

steps.action: Add garlic and tomato paste, cook 2 minutes. Increase heat to high, add both minces and cook, breaking up lumps, until deeply browned — 8–10 minutes.
tools: Large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven

steps.action: Pour in the red wine and stir, scraping up any browned bits. Let it reduce almost completely, about 3 minutes.
tools: Large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven

steps.action: Add crushed tomatoes, bay leaf, salt and pepper. Reduce heat to the lowest setting. Partially cover and simmer for 1 hour, stirring occasionally. Add a splash of water if it looks dry.
tools: Large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven

steps.action: Stir in the milk and simmer uncovered for a further 15 minutes. The ragù should be thick, glossy, and rich.
tools: Large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven

steps.action: Cook pasta in well-salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve a mug of pasta water. Drain and toss pasta with the ragù, adding pasta water as needed to loosen.
Serve in warmed bowls. Finish with freshly grated parmesan.

name: Classic Caesar Salad
summary: Crisp romaine, a bold umami-rich dressing, crunchy croutons, and shaved parmesan. No anchovies needed — the dressing gets its depth from Worcestershire and a generous amount of parmesan.
ingredients: 2 thick slices sourdough or ciabatta (for croutons)

steps.action: Tear bread into rough chunks. Toss with olive oil and rub a cut garlic clove over them. Spread on a baking tray and bake at 200°C for 10–12 minutes until deeply golden and crunchy.

Whisk together egg yolk, mustard, minced garlic, Worcestershire, and lemon juice in a small bowl. Slowly drizzle in the olive oil while whisking constantly to emulsify. Stir in grated parmesan, salt, and pepper.
Toss the romaine with enough dressing to coat every leaf. Pile into bowls, add croutons, and shower with shaved parmesan. Season with black pepper.

name: Blueberry Muffins
summary: Tall, bakery-style muffins with a golden dome, juicy blueberry pockets, and a crunchy sugar top. The trick is not overmixing the batter.

steps.action: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper liners.
Whisk together flour, caster sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
In a separate bowl, whisk oil, eggs, buttermilk, and vanilla until combined.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry. Fold with a spatula until just combined — lumps are fine, do not overmix. Gently fold in blueberries.
Divide batter evenly among the muffin cups — fill to the top. Sprinkle demerara sugar over each. Bake 18–20 minutes until a skewer comes out clean and tops are golden.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes then transfer to a wire rack. Best eaten warm.

name: Honey Garlic Chicken Stir-Fry
summary: Tender chicken and crisp vegetables tossed in a sticky, sweet-savoury honey garlic sauce. Faster than a takeaway and considerably better.
ingredients: Sesame seeds and spring onions to serve
Steamed rice or noodles to serve

steps.action: Mix soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, sesame oil, and cornstarch in a small bowl until smooth. Set aside.

Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok over the highest heat until smoking. Add chicken in a single layer. Cook without stirring for 2 minutes to get some colour, then toss and cook 2 more minutes until just cooked. Remove and set aside.
Add remaining oil to the hot wok. Stir-fry broccoli, peppers, garlic, and ginger for 3–4 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Return chicken to the wok. Pour over the sauce and toss everything together over high heat for 1–2 minutes until the sauce is thick and glossy.
Serve over steamed rice or noodles, topped with sesame seeds and sliced spring onions.

name: Creamy Homemade Hummus
summary: Ultra-smooth hummus made from scratch using the small trick of peeling chickpeas for a silky, restaurant-quality dip in under 15 minutes.
ingredients: 3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil (plus extra to drizzle)
Smoked paprika, fresh parsley, and olive oil to serve

steps.action: Optional but worthwhile: gently squeeze each chickpea to slip off its skin. The skins make hummus grainy.
Add tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, and salt to the food processor. Blend for 2 minutes until pale and creamy.
Add chickpeas and olive oil. Blend 3–4 minutes, adding ice-cold water a tablespoon at a time, until completely smooth and light. Taste and adjust lemon, salt, or garlic.
Spread into a wide bowl, making a well in the centre. Fill with olive oil, a dusting of smoked paprika, and fresh parsley. Serve with warm pita or crudités.

name: French Toast
summary: Thick slices of brioche soaked in a vanilla-custard egg mixture and pan-fried until golden and caramelised. Weekend breakfast at its finest.
ingredients: 4 thick slices brioche or challah (2–3cm thick)
Maple syrup, fresh berries, and icing sugar to serve

steps.action: Whisk together eggs, milk, cream, vanilla, cinnamon, sugar, and salt in a shallow dish until well combined.
Soak the brioche slices in the custard for 30 seconds per side, pressing gently so the bread absorbs the mixture.
Melt butter in a non-stick pan over medium heat until foaming. Cook the soaked slices 2–3 minutes per side until deeply golden and caramelised. Work in batches.
Serve immediately with maple syrup, a pile of fresh berries, and a dusting of icing sugar.
ingredients: maple syrup, fresh berries, and icing sugar

name: Tiramisu
summary: The legendary Italian dessert: espresso-soaked ladyfingers layered with a cloud-like mascarpone cream, finished with a generous dusting of cocoa. Needs overnight chilling — worth every hour.
ingredients: 3 tbsp coffee liqueur (Kahlúa or Marsala, optional)

steps.action: Brew espresso and allow to cool completely. Stir in liqueur if using. Pour into a shallow dish.
Beat egg yolks and sugar with the electric mixer on high for 4–5 minutes until the mixture is pale, thick, and falls in ribbons.
Add mascarpone to the yolk mixture and beat on low until smooth and incorporated.
In a clean bowl with clean beaters, whisk egg whites to stiff peaks. Gently fold into the mascarpone cream in three additions, keeping as much air as possible.
Quickly dip each ladyfinger in the espresso (1 second per side — don't soak) and arrange in a single layer in the dish. Spread over half the mascarpone cream.
Repeat with a second layer of dipped ladyfingers and remaining cream. Smooth the top, cover, and refrigerate for at least 6 hours (overnight is best).
Just before serving, dust generously with cocoa powder through a fine-mesh sieve.

name: Street Beef Tacos
summary: Tender, cumin-spiced minced beef in warm corn tortillas with pickled onion, fresh cilantro, and a squeeze of lime. Weeknight street food at its best.
ingredients: Hot sauce and sour cream to serve

steps.action: Quick-pickle the onion: toss diced red onion with red wine vinegar, sugar, and a pinch of salt. Set aside — it will turn pink within 10 minutes.
Heat oil in a frying pan over high heat. Add mince and cook, breaking it up, for 5–6 minutes until deeply browned in places — don't stir constantly.
Add garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, oregano, and chilli powder. Stir for 1 minute. Season well with salt and pepper.
Warm tortillas in a dry pan for 30 seconds per side or directly over a gas flame. Keep wrapped in a clean cloth to stay soft.
Fill each tortilla with beef, pickled onion, fresh cilantro, and a squeeze of lime. Serve with hot sauce and sour cream.

name: Thai Yellow Vegetable Curry
summary: A fragrant, golden curry of seasonal vegetables in creamy coconut milk, spiked with lemongrass and lime leaves. Serve over jasmine rice.
ingredients: Fresh Thai basil and toasted peanuts to serve

steps.action: Heat coconut oil over medium heat. Add curry paste and fry, stirring constantly, for 2 minutes until fragrant and deepened in colour.
Pour in coconut milk. Add lemongrass and lime leaves. Stir to combine and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add sweet potato. Simmer for 12 minutes until just tender.
Add broccoli, red pepper, and tofu. Simmer 5 minutes more. Season with soy sauce, brown sugar, and lime juice. Stir in spinach until wilted.
Remove lemongrass and lime leaves. Serve over jasmine rice, topped with Thai basil and toasted peanuts.
ingredients: fresh Thai basil and toasted peanuts

name: Classic Greek Salad
summary: Chunky tomatoes, crisp cucumber, briny olives, and a slab of feta in herb-scented olive oil. No lettuce — this is the real horiatiki.
ingredients: ½ green bell pepper (sliced into rings)
150g block of good feta (do not crumble)

steps.action: Cut tomatoes into large wedges, cucumber into thick half-moons, and pepper into rings. Slice red onion thinly.
Arrange all vegetables and olives on a serving plate. Place the whole block of feta on top — do not crumble it.
Drizzle generously with olive oil, crumble oregano over the feta, and season with salt and pepper. Serve immediately with crusty bread.

name: Overnight Oats
summary: Creamy no-cook oats assembled the night before and customised with your favourite toppings in the morning. Breakfast that's ready before you are.
ingredients: Fresh berries, banana slices, nut butter, or granola to serve

steps.action: Divide oats, chia seeds, and salt equally between two jars.
Whisk together plant milk, yogurt, maple syrup, and vanilla. Pour over the oats and stir well to combine.
Seal jars and refrigerate overnight (or at least 4 hours). In the morning, stir, add a splash more milk if too thick, and top with berries, banana, or nut butter.
ingredients: fresh berries, banana slices, nut butter, or granola

name: Classic Smash Burger
summary: Two thin beef patties smashed on a screaming-hot skillet for maximum crust, layered with American cheese, pickles, and a punchy burger sauce in a toasted brioche bun.
tools: Cast-iron skillet or heavy frying pan

steps.action: Mix mayo, ketchup, mustard, pickle brine, and smoked paprika in a small bowl. Set aside.
Divide mince into 4 loose balls (about 100g each) — do not compact them. Season the tops generously with salt and pepper.
Heat cast-iron skillet over the highest heat for 3 minutes until smoking. Toast bun cut-sides in butter until golden; set aside.
tools: Cast-iron skillet or heavy frying pan

steps.action: Place two beef balls on the hot skillet. Immediately smash flat with the spatula and hold for 10 seconds. Cook 2 minutes until edges are deeply browned. Flip, lay cheese on top, and cook 1 more minute.
tools: Cast-iron skillet or heavy frying pan

steps.action: Repeat for the second pair of patties. Build burgers: sauce on both bun halves, lettuce, double patty stack, pickles. Serve immediately.

variants.name: Veggie
variants.description: Black bean and mushroom smash patties with the same sear, same sauce, same satisfying crunch — no beef required.

steps.action: Mix mayo, ketchup, mustard, pickle brine, and smoked paprika in a small bowl. Set aside.
Mash black beans until about 80% smooth. Add mushrooms, breadcrumbs, egg, smoked paprika, cumin, salt and pepper. Mix until it holds together. Divide into 4 balls.
Heat cast-iron skillet over high heat for 3 minutes. Toast bun halves cut-side down in butter for 2 minutes until golden. Set aside.
Place two bean balls on the hot skillet. Smash flat with a spatula. Season with salt and pepper. Cook 3 minutes until a dark crust forms. Flip, lay cheese on top, cook 2 more minutes.
Build burgers: sauce on both bun halves, lettuce on the base, two veggie patties, pickles, top bun. Serve immediately.

name: Tom Yum Soup
summary: Thailand's famous hot-and-sour prawn soup — a clear, fiery broth fragrant with lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime, and fish sauce. Bold, aromatic, and ready in 30 minutes.
ingredients: 1 litre good chicken or vegetable stock
1 tbsp chilli paste in oil (nam prik pao)

steps.action: Bring stock to a boil. Add lemongrass, galangal, lime leaves, and chillies. Simmer 10 minutes to infuse.
Add mushrooms and chilli paste. Simmer 3 minutes.
Add prawns. Cook 2–3 minutes until pink and just cooked through.
Season with fish sauce, lime juice, and sugar. Taste and adjust — it should be sour, salty, and hot in equal measure. Serve topped with spring onions and cilantro.

name: Egg Fried Rice
summary: The essential use for leftover rice — high-heat wok cooking transforms cold grains into fragrant, lightly charred fried rice studded with vegetables and fluffy egg.
ingredients: 600g cold cooked jasmine rice (day-old works best)
4 spring onions (sliced, greens and whites separated)
1 tbsp oyster sauce (or hoisin for vegan)

steps.action: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok over high heat until smoking. Add eggs and scramble loosely — remove while still slightly underdone.
Add remaining oil. Stir-fry carrots and spring onion whites for 2 minutes. Add garlic and ginger, stir 30 seconds.
Add cold rice and break up any clumps. Spread across the wok and let it sit undisturbed for 1–2 minutes to get some colour, then toss. Repeat twice.
Add peas, soy sauce, oyster sauce, and white pepper. Toss to combine. Return eggs, drizzle sesame oil, and scatter spring onion greens. Toss once more and serve.

name: Eggs Benedict
summary: Perfectly poached eggs and Canadian bacon on toasted English muffins, draped in a rich, buttery hollandaise sauce. The ultimate weekend brunch.
ingredients: Chives and smoked paprika to garnish

steps.action: Make hollandaise: whisk egg yolks and lemon juice in a heatproof bowl. Set over a saucepan of barely simmering water (don't let the bowl touch the water). Whisk constantly for 3–4 minutes until thick and pale.
Remove from heat. Slowly drizzle in melted butter a few drops at a time, whisking constantly, until emulsified and thick. Add mustard, season with salt and cayenne. Keep warm.

Bring a deep pan of water to a gentle simmer. Add vinegar. Crack each egg into a small cup, stir the water to create a gentle whirlpool, and slide in one egg at a time. Poach 3 minutes for a runny yolk.
Toast English muffins. Warm bacon in the pan for 1 minute per side.
Assemble: muffin, bacon, poached egg. Spoon hollandaise generously over the top. Garnish with chives and a dusting of smoked paprika.

name: Spaghetti Carbonara
summary: The real Roman carbonara — no cream, ever. Silky spaghetti coated in a glossy egg-and-parmesan sauce with crispy guanciale. Done in 25 minutes.

steps.action: Whisk eggs, yolks, Pecorino, Parmesan, and cracked black pepper together in a large bowl until combined. Set aside.
Cook pasta in heavily salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve at least 1 cup of starchy pasta water before draining.
Meanwhile, cook guanciale in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 6–8 minutes until golden and crispy. Remove from heat.

Add hot drained pasta to the guanciale pan (off the heat). Quickly pour in the egg mixture and toss vigorously, adding pasta water a tablespoon at a time, until you have a glossy, creamy sauce that coats every strand. The residual heat cooks the eggs — never let it get too hot or they'll scramble.
Divide into warm bowls. Finish with extra Pecorino and more cracked pepper.

variants.name: Vegetarian
variants.description: Crispy smoked mushrooms replicate the savory, chewy texture of guanciale. The egg-and-cheese sauce is identical — creamy, rich, and deeply satisfying.
ingredients: 250g king oyster or shiitake mushrooms (torn into thick strips)

steps.action: Whisk eggs, yolks, Pecorino, Parmesan, and cracked black pepper together in a large bowl. Set aside.
Cook pasta in heavily salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve at least 1 cup pasta water before draining.
Heat olive oil in a wide frying pan over high heat. Add mushroom strips, smoked paprika, and soy sauce. Cook without stirring for 4–5 minutes until deeply golden and crispy at the edges.
Add hot drained pasta to the mushroom pan off the heat. Quickly pour in the egg mixture and toss rapidly, adding pasta water a splash at a time until the sauce is silky and clings to the pasta.
Divide into warm bowls. Finish with extra Pecorino and more cracked pepper.

name: Apple & Blackberry Crumble
summary: Warm, bubbling spiced apple and blackberry beneath a buttery, oat-studded crumble topping. A British classic best served with a generous pour of custard.
ingredients: 800g Bramley or Granny Smith apples (peeled, cored, sliced)
Vanilla custard or ice cream to serve

steps.action: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Toss apple slices with blackberries, caster sugar, cinnamon, ginger, and cornstarch. Pour into the baking dish.
Rub cold butter into flour and salt until the mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs. Stir in oats and demerara sugar. Don't overwork — you want clumps.
Scatter the crumble topping evenly over the fruit. Bake 35–40 minutes until the top is golden and the fruit is bubbling around the edges.
Rest for 5 minutes. Serve warm with custard or ice cream.

name: Chicken Tikka Masala
summary: Charred, yogurt-marinated chicken in a rich, creamy tomato-based masala sauce. Britain's adopted national dish — for good reason.
ingredients: Fresh cilantro and basmati rice to serve

steps.action: Combine yogurt, half the garlic and ginger, 1 tsp garam masala, cumin, turmeric, and paprika. Add chicken, toss to coat, and marinate at least 20 minutes (overnight is ideal).
Grill or bake the marinated chicken at 220°C / under a hot grill for 12–15 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges and cooked through.
Meanwhile, melt butter and oil in a heavy pan. Cook onion over medium heat 10 minutes until golden. Add remaining garlic, ginger, and spices; cook 2 minutes.
Add crushed tomatoes and simmer 10 minutes until sauce thickens. Stir in cream and season with salt.
Add grilled chicken to the sauce. Simmer 5 minutes to marry the flavours. Serve over basmati rice, topped with fresh cilantro.

name: Caprese with Burrata
summary: Ripe heritage tomatoes with creamy, molten-centred burrata, fresh basil, and aged balsamic. An Italian antipasto that is greater than the sum of its parts.
ingredients: Large handful of fresh basil leaves
1–2 tsp aged balsamic vinegar or balsamic glaze
Flaky sea salt and cracked black pepper

steps.action: Slice tomatoes into varying thicknesses — some thick rounds, some wedges. Season generously with flaky salt and let them sit for 5 minutes to draw out juices.
Arrange tomatoes on a serving plate. Tear burrata and place over the tomatoes. Scatter basil leaves.
Drizzle with olive oil and balsamic, season with cracked pepper. Serve immediately with good bread — do not refrigerate.

name: Butter Croissants
summary: Proper laminated croissants with flaky, honeycomb layers and a shattering crust. A weekend project, but the result is incomparable to anything from a packet.
ingredients: 250g cold European-style butter (82%+ fat, for lamination)

steps.action: Mix flour, yeast, salt, and sugar. Add warm milk and softened butter. Knead 8–10 minutes until smooth but not over-developed. Shape into a rectangle, wrap in clingfilm, and refrigerate 1 hour.
Beat cold butter into a 20cm square between two sheets of clingfilm using a rolling pin. Refrigerate if it warms up.

Roll chilled dough into a 40×20cm rectangle. Place butter square in the centre, fold dough over it like an envelope. Seal edges. Roll to 60×20cm, fold into thirds (letter fold). Wrap and chill 30 minutes. Repeat fold and chill twice more.

Roll final dough to 4mm thick. Cut into long triangles. Roll each from the base towards the tip, stretching slightly as you go. Place on lined baking trays, curving into a crescent. Prove at room temperature for 2 hours until puffy.
Brush gently with egg wash. Bake at 200°C for 16–18 minutes until deep mahogany brown. Cool on a rack for at least 20 minutes before eating.

name: Slow-Cooked Beef Stew
summary: Beef shin braised low and slow with root vegetables and red wine until meltingly tender. A deeply comforting one-pot meal that improves overnight.
ingredients: 800g beef shin or chuck (cut into 5cm chunks)
Mashed potato or crusty bread to serve
tools: Large Dutch oven or heavy pot

steps.action: Pat beef dry and season with salt and pepper. Toss in flour to coat. Heat oil in a Dutch oven over high heat. Brown beef in batches for 3–4 minutes per side. Remove and set aside.
tools: Large Dutch oven or heavy pot

steps.action: Reduce heat to medium. Cook onion, carrot, and celery for 8 minutes. Add garlic and tomato paste, cook 2 minutes.
tools: Large Dutch oven or heavy pot

steps.action: Pour in wine and let it bubble for 3 minutes, scraping up any browned bits. Add stock, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaves. Return beef. Bring to a simmer.
tools: Large Dutch oven or heavy pot

steps.action: Cover and cook over the lowest heat for 2 hours, stirring occasionally, until beef is fall-apart tender and sauce is rich and glossy. Remove herb sprigs. Adjust seasoning.
tools: Large Dutch oven or heavy pot

steps.action: Serve over mashed potato or with crusty bread to soak up the sauce.

name: Pad Thai
summary: Thailand's iconic stir-fried noodle dish — rice noodles, egg, tofu or prawns, and a sweet-sour tamarind sauce, finished with peanuts, lime, and bean sprouts.
ingredients: Fresh cilantro and dried chilli flakes to serve

steps.action: Soak rice noodles in cold water for 30 minutes (or follow package instructions). Drain and set aside.
Mix tamarind paste, fish sauce, oyster sauce, and sugar in a small bowl. Taste — it should be tangy, salty, and slightly sweet.
Heat oil in a wok over the highest heat. Stir-fry prawns or tofu with garlic for 2–3 minutes until cooked. Push to one side, scramble in the eggs until just set.
Add drained noodles and pour over the sauce. Toss everything together vigorously for 2–3 minutes until noodles absorb the sauce and start to caramelise slightly.
Add bean sprouts and spring onions. Toss for 30 seconds — keep them crisp. Serve immediately topped with peanuts, lime wedges, cilantro, and chilli flakes.

name: Homemade Granola
summary: Golden, clumping oat granola with nuts, seeds, and honey — infinitely better than shop-bought. Make a big batch and it keeps for two weeks.
ingredients: 100g dried fruit (raisins, cranberries, or apricots — added after baking)
Greek yogurt, plant milk, or fresh fruit to serve

steps.action: Preheat oven to 160°C. Line a large baking tray with parchment.
Combine oats, nuts, seeds, cinnamon, and salt in a large bowl. Stir in maple syrup, melted coconut oil, and vanilla until every oat is coated.
Spread in an even layer on the baking tray — press it down slightly for more clusters. Bake 25–30 minutes, rotating the tray halfway, until golden. Do not stir during baking.
Leave to cool completely on the tray without disturbing — this is how the clusters form. Once cool, break into pieces and stir in dried fruit. Store in an airtight jar.

name: Chocolate Lava Cakes
summary: Individual warm chocolate cakes with a molten, flowing centre. The batter is made ahead and refrigerated — pull them out 20 minutes before your guests arrive.
ingredients: Cocoa powder for dusting the moulds
Vanilla ice cream or crème fraîche to serve

steps.action: Butter 4 ramekins thoroughly and dust with cocoa powder, tapping out excess. Refrigerate.
Melt chocolate and butter together over a pan of barely simmering water, stirring until smooth. Cool slightly.
Beat eggs, yolks, and sugar with an electric mixer for 3–4 minutes until pale and thick. Fold in the cooled chocolate mixture, then sift in flour and salt. Fold until just combined.
Divide batter between the prepared ramekins. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (up to 24 hours). Preheat oven to 200°C when ready to bake.
Bake chilled ramekins for exactly 12 minutes — edges should be set but the centre should still wobble. Run a knife around the edge, invert onto plates, and serve immediately with ice cream.
ingredients: vanilla ice cream or crème fraîche

name: Gazpacho
summary: Andalusia's legendary chilled tomato and vegetable soup — blended smooth and served ice-cold. Intensely refreshing on a hot day, and no cooking required.
ingredients: 1 cucumber (peeled, roughly chopped, plus extra to garnish)
100ml extra-virgin olive oil (plus extra to drizzle)
3 tbsp sherry vinegar or red wine vinegar
1 thick slice day-old white bread (crusts removed, soaked in water)
Croutons, diced cucumber, and a drizzle of olive oil to serve

steps.action: Combine tomatoes, pepper, cucumber, red onion, garlic, squeezed-out soaked bread, salt, olive oil, and vinegar in a blender. Blend on high for 2 minutes until completely smooth.
Pass through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing with a ladle to extract maximum liquid. Discard the solids.
Taste and adjust seasoning and vinegar. Add ice-cold water to reach a pourable but not watery consistency. Chill for at least 1 hour — it must be served very cold.
Pour into bowls or glasses. Garnish with diced cucumber, croutons, and a generous drizzle of olive oil.

name: Roasted Pumpkin Soup
summary: Sweet roasted pumpkin blended with coconut milk and warming spices into a velvety, vibrant orange soup. Topped with toasted pumpkin seeds and a swirl of cream.
ingredients: 1.2kg pumpkin or butternut squash (peeled, seeded, cubed)
Toasted pumpkin seeds, coconut cream, and fresh chilli to serve

steps.action: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss pumpkin cubes and quartered onion with olive oil, cumin, paprika, ginger, salt, and pepper. Add unpeeled garlic cloves. Spread on a baking tray.
Roast for 35–40 minutes until pumpkin is tender and caramelised at the edges.
Squeeze garlic from their skins. Transfer all roasted vegetables and garlic to a large saucepan. Add stock and coconut milk. Blend until completely smooth.
Heat gently over medium heat. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve in warmed bowls with a swirl of coconut cream, toasted pumpkin seeds, and fresh chilli.

name: Falafel Wraps
summary: Crispy, herb-packed chickpea falafel in warm pita with tahini sauce, pickled cabbage, and fresh salad. A Middle Eastern street-food classic that's entirely vegan.
ingredients: 3 tbsp tahini + 2 tbsp lemon juice + 2 tbsp water (tahini sauce)
Shredded red cabbage, sliced tomato, cucumber, and fresh herbs to serve
tools: Large frying pan or deep pan

steps.action: Blend tahini, lemon juice, water, and a pinch of salt into a smooth sauce. Add more water if needed. Set aside.
Pulse chickpeas, onion, garlic, parsley, cilantro, cumin, coriander, and cayenne in a food processor until the mixture resembles coarse sand — not smooth. Do not over-blend.
Add flour, baking powder, salt, and pepper. Pulse to combine. Refrigerate for 20 minutes — this helps the mixture hold together.
Shape into balls (golf ball-sized). Heat 3cm of oil in a pan to 175°C. Fry in batches for 3–4 minutes until deeply golden and crispy. Drain on paper towels.
tools: Large frying pan or deep pan

steps.action: Warm pitas in a dry pan. Fill with falafel, drizzle tahini sauce, and pile in the shredded cabbage, tomato, cucumber, and fresh herbs.
